tasks.title: RPN after a mitigation
tasks.solution: RPN = S·O·D; with S and O unchanged, the RPN drops by 1 − D₂/D₁. The module's example: the BEC failure, S 9, O 3, D 6 → 3: RPN 162 → 81, minus 50 %. A detection mitigation does not change S, which is why rows with S ≥ 9 are reviewed regardless of RPN.

tasks.title: The order for closing risks
tasks.solution: RPN B = 6·4·7 = 168. RPN A = S·O·D is at most 120, so the difference is negative and by RPN row A ranks lower. But A has severity S ≥ 9, so by the course rule it is closed with a mitigation regardless of RPN (like row F-15 with RPN 60 in the module's FMEA).
